2: Start with the rule the whole profile enforces.
A partner account gets access because a sponsor asked, an approver agreed and a date was set, never because it exists or synchronized.
The partner is authoritative for the person's affiliation and the credential it issues.
The agency is authoritative for federation trust, eligibility, authorization, monitoring, review, suspension and termination.

So engineering has four things to prove for every partner: that trust is scoped to that partner alone, that every account traces to an approved request with an expiry, that every partner account is a guest unless an exception record says otherwise, and that access really ends at the last assignment and at partner exit.
The rest of this deck is how.
4: nist special publication eight hundred sixty-three, revision four, final since July 31, 2025, separates three scales.
Identity proofing is usually done by the partner, under its own practice.
Authentication is done by the partner's identity service.
Federation assurance is set by the agency, as relying party, for each application.
special publication eight hundred sixty-three C, revision four says what each federation level demands.
At level one, the identity provider signs the assertion, and the relying party validates it against the expected key, with the assertion audience-restricted and protected against replay.

Level two adds injection protection, a transaction the relying party starts, an assertion for a single relying party, a trust agreement established in advance, and identifiers without plaintext personal data.
Level three adds holder-of-key or a bound authenticator.
Selection follows nist's steps: assess impact per user group, take the initial levels, tailor, and document the result in a Digital Identity Acceptance Statement.
The chapter didn't read the October 6, 2026 planning note on special publication eight hundred sixty-three C, revision four in full, so check it first.
5: For partners outside the agency's own organization, the route is entitlement management with B to B collaboration guests.

Create one connected organization per partner, configured, never proposed: a policy open to all users creates proposed connected organizations automatically, so each partner policy targets specific connected organizations only, and a proposed one is a finding.
Create one access package per partner use case, in a catalog enabled for external users, hidden so only people with the link can find it.
Approval has two stages: the agency sponsor, then the resource owner for the higher-risk applications, with expiry at most 365 days.
When a guest loses the last assignment, sign-in is blocked and the account is deleted after 30 days.
And guests can't invite other guests.
One caution from Microsoft Learn: Conditional Access that affects guests can block My Access, so test that a partner can still request before you add an exclusion.
6: Every partner on Entra I D gets its own organization-specific entry in cross-tenant access settings.
Those settings override the defaults, and M F A and device claims from other tenants aren't trusted by default.
Inbound B to B collaboration is allowed for the partner tenant only, scoped to the access package's applications.
B to B direct connect is blocked.

Trusting the partner's M F A is turned on only where the agreement says the partner enforces it at home, and Conditional Access still requires the strength; trusting M F A only skips the second prompt.
Trust in compliant or hybrid-joined devices stays off, unless the agreement names the partner's compliance standard.
Automatic redemption stays off on the default route.
The record holds the partner's immutable tenant I D and the names it resolves to, and a partner domain that resolves to another tenant is a stop condition.
For a partner on sam-ul or WS-Fed federation, Conditional Access can require only the M F A grant, so the agreement must say whether the method is phishing-resistant.
7: No new Conditional Access policy is needed.
Five policies in the workbook's library already carry the partner tenant list.
CA009, for M F A, and CA010, for terms of use, include partner users.
CA011, CA012 and CA038 apply guest limits to everyone except the partner tenants.
The list must be identical in all five; a partner in one and not the others is a drift finding.
The identity governance officer owns it, and a partner enters it only when its access package goes lyve.
The user type decides which policies apply.
CA011, CA012 and CA038 match only guest-type external users, so an external member from an unlisted tenant escapes them.
A member also gets member-level directory permissions, and falls outside persona rules and reviews scoped to guests.
That's why partner persons are guests by default.
A read-only Graph check compares the list across the five policies and against the partner entries in cross-tenant access settings.
9: Cross-tenant synchronization pushes the partner's internal members into the agency tenant as B to B users.

Allow it only when every condition holds and is written in the exception record: the partner's people are internal members of an Entra tenant, the population is too large or changes too fast for per-person requests, the agreement covers privacy, consent and minimization, and the business owner decides, with the sponsor named.
The agency doesn't own the mappings, so it states them as terms and tests the result.
The user type mapping defaults to member; the profile requires guest, applied always.
Matching uses the alternative security identifier and can't be changed.
The deletion threshold defaults to 500, so set it below the expected population.
A failing job goes into quarantine.
Scope only assigned users and groups; nested groups don't cascade.
And cycles run every 40 minutes, so emergency suspension can't wait for one.
Sync creates the account; access still comes from an access package.
10: When the partner deletes or unassigns a user, the user is soft-deleted in the agency tenant and can be restored for 30 days.
A sign-in block set on the agency side lasts only until the source user changes, and then sync re-enables the account.
So an agency suspension of a synced user also removes their access package assignment.
A severed relationship leaves accounts behind: deleting the sync policy doesn't remove the users it created, and turning off inbound sync has no effect on users already synchronized.
To end cleanly, the partner unassigns everyone while the agency keeps inbound sync on, then the agency turns it off and deletes what remains.
On licensing, each synced user needs Entra I D P1 in the source tenant.
Cross-cloud sync carries users only, and manager isn't synced across clouds, so no approval rule may depend on a synced manager.
11: The chapter's responsibility table has one decider per row, the agency business owner, and names who does the work.
Identity engineering builds and runs the credential checks, the attribute mappings, the authentication validation and the lifecycle, including disables and reconciliation.
The sponsor does the work on eligibility, authorization and the evidence, and requests suspensions.
Security operations contains incidents first and tells the business owner after.
The I S S O is consulted on proofing, credentials, incidents and evidence, and the privacy office on attributes.
The identity governance officer owns the partner tenant list and is alerted to any change in cross-tenant settings.
On the partner's side, the partner keeps its affiliation record accurate, issues and revokes credentials, sends mover and leaver notices, and coordinates incidents under the agreement.
13: Every partner relationship has one record, written before access is granted and kept as evidence after.
It lives in the repository beside the configuration it describes, so a change to either arrives in the same pull request.
It has six sections: authority and purpose, owners, risk, agreement and assurance, route and user type, lifecycle and operations, and the readiness checks.
Three rules apply to every field.
Reference, don't copy: the agreement, the privacy determination and the records schedule go in as identifiers and dates.
One decider: each readiness check names the business owner, and the authorizing official is consulted on the last.
And a blank is a finding: write none or not applicable, with a reason.
The Entra profile adds the values the record asks for: tenant relationship, cross-tenant settings, configuration I D's, mappings, access governance, validation results and monitoring.
The record holds no personal data about individual partner persons, and no secrets.
14: The profile ships its validation tests as copy-paste Microsoft Graph PowerShell.
Run them in a test tenant with a test partner tenant first; they were checked against the Graph PowerShell reference but haven't been run against a tenant.
Test zero confirms the tenant I D resolves to the partner and that the trust and redemption values match the record.
Test one creates a guest through an access package request, and checks the user type is guest and that My Access still loads under the M F A policy.
Test two finds any partner account that isn't a guest.

Three is emergency suspension, four removes the assignment, five finds duplicates and unredeemed invitations, six proves denial for a user with no assignment and for an unlisted tenant, seven shows the M F A policy applied, eight covers devices, nine rolls back, and ten is partner exit.
Tests one, three, four, nine and ten write, and each says how to undo it.
15: Native sign-in and audit retention in Entra is 30 days, so the logs stream to the workspace.
Provisioning logs for sync liv in the partner's tenant, so the agreement has to deliver them.
On the agency side, sync changes show up in the audit log under the sync fabric actor.
Entitlement management records requests, approvals, expiries and removals.
The sign-in log shows the M F A policy's failures and any denied attempts after removal.
Cross-tenant settings changes are audited and alerted to the identity governance officer.
And drift compares the repository with the tenant: a partner list mismatch, any non-guest without a record, or trust values that differ from the record.

The profile suggests four alerts: a member partner account with no record, a sync cycle deleting more than expected, and a partner list mismatch, all high; and a cross-tenant change made outside a pull request, medium.
16: Each step maps to nist special publication eight hundred fifty-three controls, to fed-ramp Key Security Indicators where the workbook already pairs them, and to the evidence the I S S O keeps.
The partner entry and its trust settings support AC-3, AC-20 and IA-8, with test zero's output and the agreement clause behind each trust value.
The access package, its approval and expiry support A C two, with the policy export and review history.
Suspension, removal and exit support automated account disabling, and stand in for the agency's own personnel controls through the agreement.
Denial and M F A tests support IA-8 and IA-2.
Monitoring supports AU-6, and drift supports CA-7.
Key Security Indicators describe what cloud service providers report, so the agency doesn't report them; it lines its own evidence up with them.
And the cloud services involved must sit inside a fed-ramp-certified offering that the agency's own authorization relies on.
17: Last, the government-cloud check, read on November 6, 2026 and rechecked before each new partner.

For an agency tenant in G C C, entitlement management and connected organizations are available, and a partner in G C C High or D O D connects as Entra I D in another cloud, with both tenants enabling each other's cloud.
B to B direct connect isn't supported across clouds, and Teams doesn't support external members across clouds, so check each application's government service description.
Several things are honestly marked not verified.
Whether cross-cloud sync is generally available: one Microsoft page called it public preview in August 2025.
The fed-ramp boundary rules for each feature used.
The records schedules for agreements and reviews.
And the special publication eight hundred sixty-three C, revision four planning note.
Confirm each before you rely on it.
The chapter, the record and the Entra profile carry every command and footnote.
